themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Surge
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints (Uber, Lyft, etc.) spiked to 18 complaints THIS WEEK, a 269% increase from the 8-week baseline of 4.9 weekly complaints, suggesting a sudden shift in ride-hailing patterns or driver behavior in Sunnyside/Woodside.
evidence: 18 for-hire vehicle complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (269% spike, z-score: 7.16)
Spike is statistically significant with high severity classification
No prior recent news mentions or Reddit discussion, indicating newly emerging concern
reporting_angles: Interview residents and business owners on 46th Ave and Queens Blvd about what changed—are drivers parking illegally, idling, or flooding the area?
Contact TLC to determine if new driver surge, airport rerouting, or event-based traffic explains the spike

themes_detail.label: Outdoor Dining Complaints Explode
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining complaints jumped to 5 complaints THIS WEEK from a near-zero 8-week baseline (0.2 avg), a 1900% spike, suggesting rapid expansion of street dining infrastructure or neighbor backlash against new venues.
evidence: 5 outdoor dining complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1900% spike, z-score: 10.97)
Highest z-score among all recent spikes, indicating extreme deviation from baseline
Aligns with active ULURP rezonings (21-31 46th Ave, 50-02 Queens Blvd) that may be attracting new commercial activity
reporting_angles: Map where the 5 complaints originated—are they clustered around a new restaurant or a few expanding venues?
Interview residents about noise, trash, and seating overflow; contact Department of Consumer Affairs about new permits issued in past 2 weeks

themes_detail.label: Park Noise Spike
themes_detail.summary: Park noise complaints surged to 5 complaints THIS WEEK, a 700% increase from the 0.6 weekly baseline, suggesting either increased park usage, events, or unmanaged activity in Sunnyside or Woodside parks.
evidence: 5 park noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% spike, z-score: 9.04)
Community board has standing request for 'new or expanded park amenities,' suggesting underutilized or overcrowded park infrastructure
Queens CD 2 Walk to Park Site Selection is in active public review, indicating city recognition of park gaps
reporting_angles: Identify which parks generated complaints (Sunnyside Park, Bliss Park, etc.) and observe conditions firsthand during peak hours
Interview Parks Department about recent events, programming changes, or maintenance issues in the district

themes_detail.label: Panhandling Uptick Last Week
themes_detail.summary: Panhandling complaints reached 8 complaints LAST WEEK, a 2033% spike from the 8-week baseline of 0.4, suggesting a sudden increase in street solicitation or changed resident reporting behavior.
evidence: 8 panhandling complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (2033% spike, z-score: 10.96)
Second-highest z-score overall, indicating extreme statistical significance
Occurs alongside litter basket requests spike (1233%) and drinking complaints spike (433%), suggesting interconnected street activity/conditions
reporting_angles: Walk high-complaint areas (likely Queens Blvd, Skillman Ave corridor) and assess street conditions and street-level social services
Contact NYPD and local social services agencies to determine if enforcement, outreach, or shelter capacity changes triggered spike

themes_detail.label: Sanitation & Street Maintenance Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Three related complaints spiked simultaneously THIS WEEK: litter basket requests (1233% spike, 5 complaints), drinking complaints (433% spike, 6 LAST WEEK), and curb condition (273% spike, 7 LAST WEEK), suggesting systemic street cleanliness or maintenance deterioration.
evidence: Litter basket requests: 5 THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 average (1233% spike, z-score: 6.65)
Drinking complaints: 6 LAST WEEK vs. 1.1 average (433% spike, z-score: 4.18)
Curb condition: 7 LAST WEEK vs. 1.9 average (273% spike, z-score: 4.4)
Street Condition complaints remain elevated at 1386 over 90 days, indicating sustained baseline stress on infrastructure
reporting_angles: Request sanitation schedule data from DSNY to determine if street cleaning frequency changed or was disrupted in past 2 weeks
Photograph and document curb conditions and litter accumulation on major commercial corridors (Queens Blvd, 43rd Ave) for visual evidence
